title: A program can count its reach without knowing whether it solved the problem
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office synthesis of federal program performance management and evaluation evidence
geography: United States federal programs and agencies

observations.period: 2026; GAO synthesis of federal program performance management

denominator.unit: GAO synthesis of selected federal-program oversight findings

outcome_evidence.value: many programs lack clearly defined goals or relevant data to assess outcomes

decision_problem.value: Congress and agency leaders often lack information to determine whether programs solve intended problems

input_output_boundary.value: programs often focus on money spent or people reached rather than whether lives improved

observations.method: GAO synthesis of prior audits, program performance-management work, and evaluation guidance; it is not a national probability sample of federal programs.
observations.uncertainty: The synthesis identifies recurring oversight gaps but does not estimate their prevalence across all programs, quantify recipient harm, or provide a single effectiveness score.
observations.subgroup: Federal agencies and programs reviewed by GAO; selected examples include health, food, childcare, public safety, disaster, and homeland-security programs.
observations.counterinterpretation: A missing outcome measure does not prove a program failed; performance management can serve as an early-warning system and can improve before impact evidence is available.

observations.period: 2026; selected programs serving pregnant women, young children, and their families

denominator.unit: federal programs at five agencies identified by GAO as providing direct services only to this population

programs_with_performance_management.unit: programs with goals, data collection, and use of information

programs_without_performance_management.unit: programs recommended to fully develop the process

observations.method: GAO review of selected programs and their performance-management processes.
observations.uncertainty: The 15 programs are a selected review universe, not a representative sample or a causal comparison; having a performance process does not prove an outcome improved.
observations.subgroup: Pregnant women, young children, and their families as intended service population; program-level review does not observe individual recipients.
observations.counterinterpretation: Twelve programs having performance processes is evidence of measurement capacity, not evidence that those programs produced adequate or durable household outcomes.

observations.period: 2020; federal manager access to robust evaluations

denominator.unit: federal manager survey result summarized by GAO

managers_with_robust_evaluation_access.unit: share of surveyed federal managers reporting access to robust evaluations

observations.method: GAO summary of a 2020 survey of federal managers about access to robust program evaluations.
observations.uncertainty: The source summary does not reproduce the full denominator here, and the survey predates the 2026 report; it is not a current national estimate of agency evaluation capacity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Managers may use other performance information even without a robust impact evaluation; lack of access does not prove lack of all useful evidence.

observations.period: 2019-2024; DHS Securing the Cities measurement improvement

denominator.unit: DHS Securing the Cities program case summarized by GAO

2019_status.value: did not collect information to fully track cities' use of funds or assess performance

2024_status.value: established goals, performance measures, milestones, and quarterly financial assessments

preparedness_impact.unit: measured effect on nuclear-terrorism detection or deterrence

observations.method: GAO comparison of earlier oversight and subsequent follow-up on a named DHS program.
observations.uncertainty: Improved goals and tracking show management capacity, not causal improvement in preparedness, local capability, or public safety.
observations.subgroup: State and local governments participating in DHS Securing the Cities; recipient-level outcome coverage is not reported here.
observations.counterinterpretation: This is a counterexample to a simple state-failure story: oversight can lead to better measurement and management even when final impact remains open.

related_sources.claim: GAO's managing-for-results overview provides related performance-management and evaluation guidance.

boundary: This record measures federal performance-management and evaluation capacity, selected program process coverage, and one documented improvement path. It does not establish a national program-effectiveness rate, recipient-level adequacy, durable outcomes, trust change, political action, or program failure.
